issues.author: afrind
issues.body:
>  Delivery begins from the first object (object 0) of that group.

It would help if you explain how a relay in particular is expected to handle this.

It requires the relay to know if it has the entire Largest Group in cache through Largest Object, or to FETCH if it does not, right?  The _first_ relay subscriber can send Largest Group upstream (if supported), but after that, it's dicey.

comments.author: kixelated
comments.body:
Sure, going to explain it here unless you want a 2nd draft version.

The relay knows the largest group if it has an active SUBSCRIBE. Doesn't matter what the cache looks like. 

If the relay doesn't have an active SUBSCRIBE, it would start one with filter=LargestGroup. If the upstream doesn't support LargestGroup, the relay could do a JOINING FETCH, but falling back to a SUBSCRIBE filter=NextGroup may be required (ex. upstream doesn't cache).

## 🤖 Installing Claude Code GitHub App

This PR adds a GitHub Actions workflow that enables Claude Code integration in our repository.

### What is Claude Code?

[Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code) is an AI coding agent that can help with:
- Bug fixes and improvements  
- Documentation updates
- Implementing new features
- Code reviews and suggestions
- Writing tests
- And more!

### How it works

Once this PR is merged, we'll be able to interact with Claude by mentioning @claude in a pull request or issue comment.
Once the workflow is triggered, Claude will analyze the comment and surrounding context, and execute on the request in a GitHub action.

### Important Notes

- **This workflow won't take effect until this PR is merged**
- **@claude mentions won't work until after the merge is complete**
- The workflow runs automatically whenever Claude is mentioned in PR or issue comments
- Claude gets access to the entire PR or issue context including files, diffs, and previous comments

### Security

- Our Anthropic API key is securely stored as a GitHub Actions secret
- Only users with write access to the repository can trigger the workflow
- All Claude runs are stored in the GitHub Actions run history
- Claude's default tools are limited to reading/writing files and interacting with our repo by creating comments, branches, and commits.
- We can add more allowed tools by adding them to the workflow file like:

```
allowed_tools: Bash(npm install),Bash(npm run build),Bash(npm run lint),Bash(npm run test)
```

There's more information in the [Claude Code action repo](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code-action).

After merging this PR, let's try mentioning @claude in a comment on any PR to get started!

## Summary
This PR introduces graceful session shutdown and migration capabilities to moq-lite, along with a clarifying rename of the announce subscription message.

## Key Changes
- **Added GOAWAY stream (0x5)**: Enables either endpoint to initiate graceful session shutdown with optional redirect to a new session URI. Peers receiving a GOAWAY must not open new streams and should migrate active subscriptions if a new URI is provided.
- **Renamed ANNOUNCE_PLEASE to ANNOUNCE_SUBSCRIBE**: More accurately reflects the purpose of the message as a subscription request for broadcast announcements rather than a request for information.
- **Updated documentation**: Added comprehensive section describing GOAWAY stream behavior, message format, and migration semantics.
- **Updated changelog**: Added moq-lite-04 entry documenting these changes.
- **Updated comparison tables**: Removed GOAWAY from "Deleted Messages" section and updated message rename references.

## Implementation Details
- GOAWAY message format includes a Message Length field and optional New Session URI string field
- Empty URI string indicates no redirect; peer should simply close the session
- Sender closes the stream (FIN) when ready to terminate the session
- Peer should close all streams and session after migrating or when no longer needed
- Stream type 0x5 is reserved for GOAWAY, with either endpoint able to initiate

pulls.body:
## Summary

Three additions for moq-lite-05:

### 1. REANNOUNCE (atomic re-announcement)
A new `restart` (2) value for `Announce Status` on the existing ANNOUNCE message. Semantically equivalent to `ended` immediately followed by `active` for the same path, but signals that the broadcast was never actually unavailable — useful when only the origin or hop path changes (relay failover, upstream restart). The Hop ID list may differ from the prior announcement.

Alternation rules updated: a broadcast cycles `ended` ↔ (`active`|`restart`). A `restart` without a prior `active` is a protocol violation.

### 2. Timestamps and per-track timescale
Based on [moq-dev/moq#1439](https://github.com/moq-dev/moq/pull/1439).

- `Publisher Timescale (i)` added to SUBSCRIBE_OK. Units per second; `0` means unspecified. Fixed for the lifetime of the subscription.
- `Timestamp Delta (i)` prepended to every FRAME — zigzag-encoded signed delta from the previous frame's timestamp (first frame deltas from `0`).
- Expiration is now timestamp-based when timescale is non-zero, falling back to wall-clock arrival time otherwise. This keeps expiration consistent across relays and unaffected by buffering/jitter.

### 3. QUIC datagram delivery
Based on [moq-dev/moq#1374](https://github.com/moq-dev/moq/pull/1374), but with a different shape per discussion: no separate DATAGRAMS control stream. A publisher MAY send any group as one QUIC datagram routed via the existing Subscribe ID, so datagrams and streams coexist on a single subscription.

Datagram body: `Subscribe ID (i) | Group Sequence (i) | Timestamp (i) | Payload (b)`. Each datagram is a complete group with exactly one frame; not cached, not retransmitted. Total body capped at 1200 bytes to fit within the minimum QUIC path MTU without IP fragmentation — oversize payloads must be sent as a Group Stream instead. Subscribers must deduplicate by group sequence when receiving both delivery paths.

## Open design choices worth a second look

- Status name `restart` vs `reannounce` — happy to rename.
- Datagram includes an absolute `Timestamp` (PR 1374 omits it) so timestamp-based expiration also works for datagram-only groups.
- No separate DATAGRAMS control stream / no per-subscription opt-out. Could add a SUBSCRIBE flag if subscribers need to refuse datagrams.

## Test plan

- [x] `make draft-lcurley-moq-lite.txt` builds cleanly.
- [ ] Cross-check wire formats against the moq-dev Rust implementation once Lite05 lands there.
- [ ] Working group review of the `restart` naming and the datagram-MTU cap.
